focus: Hard-rule enforcement sweep for cli-codex, cli-cursor, cli-claude-code, cli-devin and cli-pi against buildLineageCommand and the per-kind adapters in fanout-run.cjs.

label: drift: cli-codex SKILL.md:165 declares the -c service_tier="fast" flag an ALWAYS rule, but buildCodexLineageCommand emits it only when lineage.serviceTier is set (fanout-run.cjs:2335); with serviceTier null in the run config every codex lineage silently falls back to the caller ~/.codex/config.toml default. The key is absent from cli-codex/hard-rules.json, so the rule engine cannot judge it either. Introduced with the codex service-tier forwarding.

drift/bug: cli-devin SKILL.md:243 makes "-- before every print-mode prompt" a dispatch-critical gotcha, but buildDevinLineageCommand composes ['-p', prompt, '--model', model] at fanout-run.cjs:2807 with no separator and the file contains no inserted '--' anywhere; the rule is also absent from cli-devin/hard-rules.json, so a prompt starting with "-" is parsed as CLI flags and nothing catches it. Introduced with the devin adapter.

improvement: stdin-redirect-required is enforced for all five executors but by three mechanisms the rule text cannot express — input:undefined turns stdio[0] to ignore (fanout-run.cjs:2114, claude 2377, cursor 2713, devin 2823), input:'' pipes-and-ends (pi 2930), and codex must feed the prompt through stdin via the trailing - arg (2342/2337) where the literal </dev/null the rule demands would break the dispatch. Outcome correct, declared wording false for two of three.

drift: the only warn-severity rule among the five sidecars, cli-claude-code non-interactive-permission-mode-risk, is unenforced and unreported — buildClaudeLineageCommand forwards --permission-mode resolvedPermission (fanout-run.cjs:2361) and never adds --dangerously-skip-permissions (all three such sites belong to native/opencode), and no lineage event or stderr note records that the deadlock risk was taken, so a hung claude leaf is indistinguishable from a slow one. Enforced count: 11 of 12 for these five packets, mirroring 12 of 13 for cli-deepseek-harness.

over-engineering/extension: the dispatch rule set is triplicated across hard-rules.json (consumed only by the hook preflight, never by the fan-out builder), SKILL.md prose, and hand-coded builder branches, with no parity check — F1 and F2 are prose-only and unenforced, F4 is sidecar-present and unreported. Removing the sidecar breaks nothing in the fan-out path; the durable fix is a parity gate asserting each sidecar id has a builder check, plus sidecar entries for the two prose-only rules.

direction: Per-executor stdin-redirect is an unenforced rule class (the deepseek sweep left one open).
reason: All five adapters close stdin, by input:undefined/ignore or input:''/end; the residual is wording, not enforcement (f-iter020-003).

label: Which declared hard rules lack runtime enforcement?
